summary.headline: Tata Power Q4 FY26 PAT rose 8% to INR1,416 crores and FY26 PAT topped INR5,000 crores, with FY27 capex guided at about INR25,000 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 EBITDA up about 10% to INR4,216 crores and PAT up 8% to INR1,416 crores, with full-year EBITDA up about 11% to INR16,090 crores and PAT above INR5,000 crores for the first time. Mundra was offline for nine months, and its SPPA with Gujarat is now signed, with four other states expected to follow in 4 to 6 weeks. FY26 capex came in well below the earlier guidance as transmission and right-of-way delays pushed projects out of the quarter. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR25,000 crores and about 2.5 GW of renewable commissioning, with roughly half of the 5 GW under-implementation pipeline due in FY27 and the rest by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up ~10% from INR3,829 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: Above INR5,000 crores (first full year above INR5,000 crores)

financial_highlights.metric: Solar cell and module manufacturing PAT (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: more than double the previous year

segments.name: Solar cell and module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR857 crores, more than double the prior year; plant stabilised with good yields. Captive demand from in-house utility-scale and rooftop projects is expected to absorb output.

segments.name: Odisha DISCOMs
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR809 crores vs INR439 crores in FY25. Management expects FY27 to be the best year for Odisha, with AT&C losses to fall about 2 percentage points a year to 12-13% over 4-5 years.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: FY26 PAT of INR499 crores with installations doubling; management targets 20% market share in 3 years and 50-60% rooftop market growth in FY27. Rooftop share was about 40% on 1.7 GW executed in FY26, per analyst.

segments.name: Utility-scale renewables / IPP
segments.commentary: Management expects about 2.5 GW commissioning in FY27 (solar 1.5-1.8 GW, remainder wind and hybrid/FDRE), with 5 GW under implementation, all in-house, and no third-party EPC work in FY27.

segments.name: Tata Projects
segments.commentary: Losses attributed to legacy projects (DFC and Barmer refinery), now largely complete. Management expects a return to profit in FY27.

segments.name: Mumbai Transmission and IEL
segments.commentary: Q4 PAT lifts of about INR50 crores (Mumbai Transmission) and INR63 crores (IEL) were attributed to asset capitalisation and deferred tax; Mumbai Transmission adds about INR1,000 crores capex a year on a 70:30 debt-equity structure.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex about INR25,000 crores, and similar capital outlay expected in FY28, covering solar, wind, pumped storage, pure hydro and transmission.
FY27 renewable commissioning about 2.5 GW (solar 1.5-1.8 GW), with a larger chunk from hybrid and FDRE projects.
Mundra SPPAs: Gujarat signed; remaining four states expected within 4-6 weeks; plant operating under Section 11 with billing per SPPA.
Odisha FY27 expected to be the best year yet, with AT&C losses falling toward 12-13% over 4-5 years.
Rooftop solar expected to grow 50-60% in FY27. Indian-made cell and module mandatory for government-subsidised rooftop from 1 June 2026.
Nuclear: 2 x 220 MW small modular reactor DPRs with NPCIL, some expected within about 6 months.

Current pipeline of 26.3 GW including existing capacity (16.7 GW operating): includes 2,800 MW Shirwata pumped hydro and Bhutan hydro (600 MW plus 1,125 MW, World Bank financing signed); Bhutan 1,125 MW expected around FY31-32.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR13,000 crores, below the guidance of about INR22,000 crores given in November; projects slipped due to right-of-way and TBCB transmission delays.
About 600 MW of large utility-scale projects being pushed to complete in Q1 FY27; deferred projects to be completed in FY27.
5 GW of renewable projects under implementation, all in-house; about 50% due in FY27 and the balance by FY28.
Company will not commission projects without permanent GNA and transmission certainty, which deferred some FY26 capex.
10 GW wafer and ingot plant to start in two phases, to supply Indian-made wafers from 1 June 2028.
Net renewable capacity: 16.7 GW operating; 26.3 GW including the current pipeline.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew about 2% in the last quarter but rose 5-6% from April; peak demand reached 256 GW and management expects it to exceed 270 GW in the next 1-2 months due to heatwave and El Nino.
Indonesian coal prices expected to stay within plus or minus 5%; coal and shipping costs have risen only slightly in the last two months.
Coal cost is a pass-through under the Gujarat SPPA, including FOB cost changes such as export duties or royalties.
Curtailment is intermittent and varies by location (evacuation allowed between 20% and 80%); cost reimbursed under GNA where curtailment occurs.
Solar and wind tenders: management says most of the current project pipeline bids with domestic cell and module requirements.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 capex well below the INR25,000 crore guidance from the November analyst meet, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance was closer to INR22,000 crores; projects slipped due to right-of-way and TBCB transmission delays. FY27 capex is about INR25,000 crores, with deferred projects completed this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full benefit of prior-period regulatory orders in Delhi distribution, and should FY27 reported numbers decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 regulatory approvals reflected INR783 crores vs INR333 crores in FY25. Further approvals are expected but are hard to quantify, as they relate to a pipeline of contested regulatory assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 IPP RE capacity addition and will the modules and cells be sourced in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 2 GW of commissioning in FY27, possibly slightly higher, of which solar is 1.5-1.8 GW. The in-house cell and module plant will supply the captive requirement, with about 1.4x module/cell content per MW.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the regulatory asset wind-down in Delhi is progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator has committed in an affidavit to amortise the regulatory assets over six years up to 2032, which is under monitoring by the Supreme Court and APTEL.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tata Power sacrifice coal profitability under the Gujarat SPPA, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said details will be shared once all five procurers sign, with no quantification given at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 5 GW renewable pipeline represent installed or contracted capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is on installed capacity; contracted capacity is lower (about 1,200 MW for FDRE and hybrid wind per the slide cited by the analyst).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR250 crore deferred tax asset and the Q4 PAT lifts at IEL and Mumbai Transmission?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the deferred tax was recognised in Q4 based on better profit visibility and carry-forward losses. IEL uplift was from a plant commissioning; Mumbai Transmission's recurring uplift is from about INR1,000 crores of annual capex.

risks_watch: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores is nearly double FY26 actual; slippage risk from transmission and right-of-way delays has already caused one shortfall.
Regulatory prior-period gains (INR783 crores in FY26) are lumpy and hard to forecast, so FY27 reported Delhi distribution profit could fall.
Four remaining Mundra SPPAs (states other than Gujarat) are not yet signed; billing is under Section 11 pending approvals.
Curtailment on solar projects and temporary GNA issues could hold back commissioning and PLF.
Coal monetisation remains open; management said a sale depends on valuation and signing all SPPAs.
Net debt to underlying EBITDA of 3.3x with a large capex programme; management says leverage discipline will be maintained.
Possible Indonesian coal export duty or royalty changes; coal cost is a pass-through under the SPPA.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating performance and growth, with cautious language on timing: management acknowledged FY26 capex shortfall and project slippage, and was evasive on quantifying regulatory gains, the coal monetisation and the Gujarat SPPA's profit-sharing terms.
key_quotes: We have now concluded the SPPA with Gujarat, and we are in the process of finalizing it with all the other 4 states, which we expect in next 4 to 6 weeks, we will complete.
Our leverage ratios are very stable. Our net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.3 and our net debt to equity is 1.2, which is very competitive for infrastructure and power industry.
We have fallen short because some of the projects that we were planning to execute in the last quarter could not happen.
So now we are being extra careful, and that is why some of our capex, which we had planned last year got deferred because we do not want to set up the plant and be on temporary GNA.
Mumbai transmission adds every year INR1,000 crores of capex. So, on a 70-30, you will have a return on equity on 30%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose about 10% to INR4,216 crores and FY26 EBITDA rose about 11% to INR16,090 crores, helped by Odisha DISCOM PAT of INR809 crores (vs INR439 crores) and rooftop PAT of INR499 crores, with the Mundra SPPA restoring coal pass-through earnings once all states sign.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (Q1-Q4 FY27), with about 600 MW pushed into Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management guides about 2.5 GW renewable commissioning in FY27 (solar 1.5-1.8 GW) from 5 GW under implementation, about half due in FY27, but FY26 capex was about INR13,000 crores against a INR22,000 crores guide, so slippage risk is material.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Rooftop installations doubled to about 1.7 GW executed in FY26 and management guides 50-60% rooftop market growth in FY27, with power demand up 5-6% from April and peak demand expected above 270 GW.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores and a similar outlay in FY28 is already guided, and a 10 GW wafer/ingot plant is planned to supply Indian-made wafers from 1 June 2028, though no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects Odisha FY27 to be its best year and further Delhi regulatory approvals are expected, but these are lumpy and hard to quantify, after FY26 regulatory approvals of INR783 crores vs INR333 crores.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crores is nearly double FY26 actual, and FY26 regulatory gains of INR783 crores are lumpy, so reported Delhi distribution profit could fall; curtailment and transmission/GNA delays could also hold back commissioning.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY27 onward; wafer plant from 1 June 2028
rows.why: Indian-made cell and module become mandatory for government-subsidised rooftop from 1 June 2026, and the in-house cell and module plant (FY26 PAT INR857 crores, more than double) is set to supply captive demand.

rows.label: Mundra SPPAs with other four states
rows.why: Gujarat SPPA is signed and the plant is operating under Section 11 with billing per SPPA, and management expects the remaining four states to follow in 4-6 weeks, though coal monetisation depends on signing all five.

rows.label: Delhi regulatory asset amortisation to 2032
rows.why: The regulator has committed in an affidavit to amortise regulatory assets over six years up to 2032, though the schedule is under Supreme Court and APTEL monitoring.

rows.label: Tata Projects return to profit
rows.why: Losses came from legacy DFC and Barmer refinery projects that are now largely complete, and management expects a return to profit in FY27.
